questions.q: An SRE team already builds Grafana dashboards. They want pipeline metrics from CloudWatch and Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus in one dashboard, with SSO sign-in and no servers to patch or scale. Which option fits?

options.why: Wrong: native and simple, but AWS-only and not Grafana, so the team cannot reuse its Grafana dashboards and Prometheus workflow.
Wrong: gives more control, but the team must provision, patch and scale the servers.
Right: fully managed Grafana workspaces with CloudWatch and Prometheus data sources and SSO through IAM Identity Center or SAML.
Wrong: it is BI for business data, not operational time-series dashboards.

questions.explain: Grafana users + AWS and Prometheus metrics + no hosting: Amazon Managed Grafana.
questions.remember: Teams that want Grafana dashboards over many AWS and open-source sources without running servers → Amazon Managed Grafana.
variants: Only AWS service metrics are needed → CloudWatch dashboards.
Business users need self-service BI → QuickSight.
Log search and analytics on OpenSearch data → OpenSearch Dashboards.

questions.q: A data platform runs pipelines in 12 accounts in one AWS Organization. Operations wants a single Amazon Managed Grafana dashboard showing CloudWatch metrics from all of them. How should the workspace get access to the data?

options.t: Use organization access mode, or a customer-managed role that assumes cross-account roles
options.why: Right: both give the workspace cross-account data access for a single multi-account dashboard.

options.t: Create one Grafana workspace per account and share links
options.why: Wrong: it does not give one pane, and more workspaces mean more user licenses to pay for.

options.t: Keep current-account mode with the service-managed role
options.why: Wrong: that role only covers data sources in the workspace's own account.

options.t: Create local Grafana users in each account
options.why: Wrong: Managed Grafana has no local users, and users do not grant data access anyway; sign-in is via IAM Identity Center or SAML.

questions.explain: Multi-account dashboards need organization mode or customer-managed cross-account roles.
questions.remember: Dashboards across several accounts → organization access mode or a customer-managed role with cross-account assumable roles. Service-managed is the easy single-account option.
variants: Only one account and the easiest setup → service-managed permissions.
Fine-grained, least-privilege policies are required → customer-managed role.
Users cannot sign in → check their assignment to the workspace or the Identity Center group.

questions.q: An Amazon Managed Grafana panel that queries a PostgreSQL database in a private subnet keeps timing out. The CloudWatch panels in the same workspace work. What should the team configure?

options.why: Wrong: that fixes empty CloudWatch panels, and CloudWatch already works here.

options.t: Move the database to a public subnet
options.why: Wrong: it exposes the database and weakens security when a private path exists.

options.t: Add a Viewer license for the dashboard user
options.why: Wrong: licenses control who can view or edit, not network reach to a data source.

options.t: A VPC connection for the workspace, with the right private subnets and security groups
options.why: Right: without a VPC connection the workspace cannot reach data sources in private subnets.

questions.explain: Private-subnet data source: give the workspace a VPC connection and check subnets, security groups, routes and DNS.
questions.remember: A data source in a private subnet → VPC connection for the workspace. Timeouts afterwards → check the connection's subnets, security groups, routes and DNS.
variants: A CloudWatch panel shows no data → the role lacks `cloudwatch:GetMetricData`, or the wrong Region or account is selected.
An Athena panel errors → workgroup or output bucket permissions, Glue catalog access or Lake Formation.
Alerts are not delivered → contact point misconfiguration or SNS permissions.

questions.q: A company gives 300 staff access to Amazon Managed Grafana. Only 10 engineers build dashboards; everyone else just looks at them. The bill is high. What is the best cost fix?

options.t: Create a separate workspace for each team
options.why: Wrong: users are billed per workspace, so more workspaces do not lower cost; share dashboards instead.

options.t: Give the viewing staff Viewer licenses and keep Editor only for the builders
options.why: Right: Viewer is about $5 per active user per month versus about $9 for Editor or Admin.

options.t: Raise dashboard refresh frequency so users log in less
options.why: Wrong: users still count as active when they log in once in the month, and frequent refreshes raise data source query costs.

options.t: Add Enterprise plugins to every user
options.why: Wrong: Enterprise plugins add about $45 per user, raising cost.

questions.explain: Most users only view: assign Viewer licenses; Editor/Admin costs more.
questions.remember: Managed Grafana bills per active user per workspace per month, with Editor/Admin dearer than Viewer. Give view-only users Viewer and remove inactive users.
variants: Many users are inactive → remove them; users count only if they log in or call the API in the month.
Athena panels drive cost → cache heavy queries; scan costs are billed by Athena, not Grafana.
Automation uses API keys or service accounts → they are billed like users.
